report.verdict: A marketing manager with strong lifecycle results, hidden behind a generic headline and About section.
write_up: You’re a marketing manager running lifecycle email and SMS for a camping gear brand, with a team and a paid social budget. A recruiter could message you based on that work, even though the headline and About don’t do it justice.
The welcome series is the model: you say what you rebuilt and how the first-purchase rate changed. The subscriber count and Klaviyo migration are also useful details already on your profile.

Start by bringing the lifecycle work into your headline and About. Then fill in the Lumen Street accounts and reports, and replace the soft skill among your top three. That gives someone hiring for lifecycle marketing a clear reason to look at your work.

cards.line: Marketing Manager | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.cannot_tell: The adjectives could belong to almost any marketer. You run lifecycle email and SMS for 410,000 subscribers, and that work belongs beside your title.
cards.example: Marketing Manager | Lifecycle email and SMS | Klaviyo
cards.question: Which lifecycle campaigns do you spend the most time running?

cards.line: Results-driven marketing professional with 8+ years of experience driving growth across multiple channels. Passionate about building brands people love and leading high-performing teams.
cards.cannot_tell: “Results-driven” skips the result you already have. Open with the camping gear audience and the welcome series instead.
cards.example: I run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand with 410,000 subscribers. I rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.question: What other lifecycle campaigns have you built alongside the welcome series?

cards.line: Rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to model! It names the work you changed and the first-purchase rate that followed.

cards.line: Supported client accounts and helped with reporting.
cards.cannot_tell: “Supported” and “helped” leave the accounts and reports unnamed. Keep those ownership words, then say what your part involved.
cards.example: Supported [number] client accounts and helped with [which reports] for [types of clients].
cards.question: What kinds of client accounts did you support, how many, and which reports did you help prepare?

cards.cannot_tell: Leadership is broad. SMS is already part of your current work and is a more specific choice for one of the three skills shown.
cards.question: What SMS work do you handle within the lifecycle program?

fit.why: Your headline and current Fernhill job name you as a Marketing Manager, with lifecycle email, SMS and paid social work.
fit.level: manager, the Marketing Manager title and two marketing specialists you manage
fit.note: “Marketing Manager” is in your headline and current title. “Lifecycle email” and “SMS” are in your current job description. “Klaviyo” is in your Senior Marketing Specialist description, and “paid social” is in your current job. Someone hiring for this work may also search for segmentation and A/B testing; neither term appears on your profile. Add them if they describe your work. Move lifecycle email and SMS into your headline.
